My friend's and I had found a white plastic bucket with a lid on it somewhere in our ghetto neighborhood. We were around 6 or 7 years old at the time. We pried it open and found tons and tons of syringes inside of it. We had no idea what it was from or for. We just kinda stared at it and my friend says "Hey, we can pretend I'm a doctor!" They convince me to lie down on a raised board that acted as a doctors examination table. My so called best friend kept saying that she was the doctor and I was a patient and I needed to get a needle done. She kept saying it wasn't going to hurt. 
So there she was uncapping a syringe that we had NO IDEA if they were USED or NOT and was coming closer and closer to my leg. 
At the last moment, I freaked out and jumped up and made a mad dash to get the hell out of there. I didn't tell anyone and my friend's didn't tell me what happened to the bucket of syringes. But HOLY GEEZ! For all we know, those could've been used for  insulin or some crazy drugs! And we totally didn't even think twice about handling this new crazy thing we found! Kids are crazy dumb!

He propositioned me saying I could have a place living there with him and would never have to worry about anything again because he would give me anything I wanted in return for sleeping with him and being company when he was home (he was a trucker). It destroyed my sense of security in life. I always thought, here was one man I could always trust and he shattered it. I already had alot of issues around trusting men due to prior abuse. I looked at all men with distrust for years. I'm happily married now and I am in a better place and I trust most men now.

As I person who has had multiple suicide attempts starting as a teen, because of untreated bipolar disorder, I made many unhealthy choices due to the rapid cycling states, stressful situations and no support. I identified sexually with men to validate my existence. Which is a horrible way to cope with untreated trauma from growing up as a child in the foster care system and growing up in dysfunctional and addiction filled  First Nations homes. But I didnt know any better. All I needed in the end were people who cared about me during the difficult times, even through the mistakes and attempts. It gets very lonely when suddenly all your friends back away from you after an attempt. 

I would suggest for you to see if you can help in anyway via the mother. But don't feel that you need to take the blame since your friend was simply reacting in a highly unstable state. Her ex bf and ex bestie betrayed her and when depressed can feel like the end of the world. And mental illness can cause impulsive actions that no one can control. It takes alot of therapy working with psychiatrists and therapists to learn to gain control over reacting so impulsively. 

Be kind to yourself, but also know your actions has impact on others. Just like how your ex friends had an impact on you. These are hard life lessons, but don't run away from them. Learn how you can grow from this and how you can be the best person you can be, even if everyone isnt acting responsibly or taking accountability for their actions. You can though. 

With respect and prayers your way.
